patients.summary: Young warehouse loader and daily smoker who joined in 2020 with no problems. A left varicocele found in 2022 was managed conservatively, flared in 2025 (seen first in an ED), and was repaired microsurgically in spring 2026; the practice heard about the surgery from him before any note arrived.

documents.title: New patient intake
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller wants to establish here. Previous primary care office was across town, last physical there roughly two years back. Works days at a distribution warehouse, needs early morning slots. Booked new patient physical 9/16 at 7:40. Faxed records release to former office today. Insurance card copied from portal upload.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
24 y/o man here to set up primary care. No complaints today.

PMH: nothing chronic. No hospitalizations. PSH: none.
Meds: none, no supplements.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family: dad diagnosed with lung cancer at 52. Paternal grandfather had COPD. Mom on thyroid replacement for hypothyroidism. No siblings with medical issues that he knows of.
Social: single, rents an apartment. Loads trucks at a distribution warehouse, lots of lifting. Smokes a pack a day, started around 16. Beer once or twice a week, no binge pattern. No other substances.

ROS negative, including cough, dyspnea, weight change, GU symptoms.

Exam: well appearing. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, thyroid not enlarged. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear, good air movement. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. GU deferred at his preference. Skin without lesions. Normal gait, normal affect.

A/P
1. Preventive care, age 24. Baseline CBC, CMP and lipids. One-time HIV and hep C screens, he agrees. Tdap today, last one he can recall was in high school. Flu shot today.
2. Tobacco use, ~8 pack-years. Talked about it plainly given his father. He says he has thought about quitting but the breaks at work are when everyone smokes. Not ready for a date. Gave quitline number. Will keep asking.
3. Records requested from prior office.
RTC one year.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Cameron, everything from Wednesday came back fine: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, sugar and cholesterol all in the normal range, and the HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to do except keep thinking about the cigarettes. Good to meet you.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Brings up something at the end of the intake: since about May he gets a dull ache on the left side of the scrotum. Worst at the end of a ten-hour shift on his feet, gone by the time he has been lying down for a while. No injury he can think of. No fever, burning with urination or discharge. Hasn't noticed a lump himself, says 'it just feels heavy.'

Otherwise well. No meds, NKDA. Smoking unchanged at a pack a day, about 10 pack-years now. Not ready.

Exam: well. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, no hernia on cough either side. GU exam standing: there is a soft fullness above the left testis that is easier to feel standing than supine. Both testes normal in size and consistency, nontender. Right side unremarkable. No inguinal nodes.

A/P
1. Left scrotal ache with supratesticular fullness. Most likely a varicocele by feel. Referring to urology to confirm and image. Briefs instead of boxers in the meantime if it helps.
2. Preventive: CBC, CMP, lipids. Flu and bivalent COVID booster today.
3. Tobacco use: counseled again, declines help for now.
RTC 1 yr, sooner as needed.

conditions.label: Varicocele
conditions.note: left; confirmed by ultrasound at urology

reports.text:
Indication: left scrotal ache, palpable supratesticular mass.
Technique: grayscale and color Doppler imaging of both hemiscrota, supine at rest and with Valsalva.
Findings: Both testes are normal in size with homogeneous echotexture and symmetric flow. Epididymides unremarkable. No hydrocele. On the left, the veins of the pampiniform plexus are dilated and show reversal of flow with Valsalva. The right pampiniform plexus is normal.

documents.title: Urology consultation
documents.author: urology
documents.body:
Outside urology group
Date of visit: 11/25/2022
Referral: primary care, left scrotal discomfort.

Thank you for sending this 26-year-old warehouse worker. For about six months he has had a mild, dull left scrotal ache that builds with long periods of standing and eases when he lies down. He feels a lumpy fullness above the testicle at times. He denies trauma, fevers, dysuria or urethral discharge.

PMH unremarkable. No medications. No known drug allergies. Family history notable for paternal lung cancer at 52, COPD in the paternal grandfather, hypothyroidism in his mother. He smokes one pack daily for the past ten years and drinks one to two drinks a week.

Exam: Irregular mass palpable superior to the left testis, enlarging with Valsalva, not transilluminating. Testes descended bilaterally and normal to palpation. Remainder of the exam normal.

Scrotal ultrasound in clinic: dilated left pampiniform plexus veins with flow reversal during Valsalva; testes normal.

Impression: Left varicocele, mildly symptomatic.

Plan: We talked through what a varicocele is and that it is common and usually harmless. For now, conservative care: snug supportive underwear, getting off his feet on breaks where possible. If the ache worsens or begins to limit work, he should come back to discuss repair. No medication prescribed. Follow up as needed.

documents.title: Urology note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got the urology note. It confirms a left varicocele, which is a widened group of veins above the testicle, and the testicles themselves looked normal on the ultrasound. Their plan of supportive underwear and seeing them again if it gets worse makes sense to me. Nothing you need to do with us.
